text: The Leaning Tower of Pisa started tipping over when it was only two or three floors tall.
Pisa, eleven seventy-three. A heavy marble bell tower, on soft clay and sand, with a foundation only about three meters deep.
Within a few years, one side was sinking.
Then Pisa went to war with its neighbours, and building stopped for almost a hundred years.
Which, by accident, saved it. The soil had time to settle and firm up.
When the builders came back, they made the new floors taller on the short side. So the tower curves, like a banana.
The bells went on top in thirteen seventy-two. And it kept on leaning.
By nineteen ninety, it leaned about five and a half degrees, and they closed it.
Engineers stacked hundreds of tonnes of lead on the high side, then gently drilled soil out from underneath.
Luckily, it worked. The top came back about forty centimeters. Unluckily, it's still leaning. On purpose, this time.
Tourists still line up to hold it up. Technically, they're not helping.
